Goodwill balance dropped from $633.8M (Jan 3, 2026) to $475.8M (Apr 4, 2026) after the Q1 FY26 charge alone; cumulative impairment from acquisitions (mainly the Apr 2024 United Grocery Outlet/Bargain Barn acquisition for which the Company paid $62M, but goodwill carry stretched higher post-business combination accounting) is materially understated by the 10-K's framing.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K's annual-cycle 'fourth quarter goodwill impairment' framing implies normalized cyclical review, but the Q1 FY26 follow-on impairment 70 days later proves the goodwill was still over-valued at Jan 3, 2026. Mode B catch: the 10-K's note on the FY25 charge does NOT alert readers that a triggering event was likely already crystallizing into Q1 FY26 (the stock had collapsed further by Mar 4, 2026 filing date). This is a SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY because the issuer recognized $158M MORE impairment in the very next quarter - the FY25 charge was insufficient. Note that current goodwill of $475.8M still carries acquisition premium from the UGO purchase that the issuer continues to defend; risk of an additional impairment in FY26 is non-trivial if comparable store sales remain negative.

rfm_tuples.f: Verify covenant compliance trajectory at cutoff and quantify cushion erosion.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Note 6 Long-term Debt + Q1 FY26 10-Q Note 6) + cash-flow trajectory
rfm_tuples.M_value: Total funded debt: $493.8M (term $273.8M + revolver $220.0M) at Jan 3, 2026. Adjusted EBITDA FY25 = $254.3M, so Total Net Leverage Ratio approximately = ($493.8M - $69.6M cash) / $254.3M = 1.67x - well within the 3.25x cap, with substantial cushion (~$378M of EBITDA-equivalent headroom). Q1 FY26 Adjusted EBITDA $43.1M vs $51.9M Q1 FY25 (-17% Y/Y); Adjusted net income $4.6M vs $13.0M (-65% Y/Y) - adjusted figures still positive but compressing. Revolver borrowed in FY25 net +$30M, suggesting working-capital draw to fund Optimization Plan cash outflows. Q1 FY26 cash and equivalents: $59.0M (down from $69.6M at Jan 3, 2026). Q1 FY26 operating cash flow +$52.6M was solid.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Leverage is real (~1.7x on adjusted EBITDA, $493.8M of total debt) but well-cushioned vs the 3.25x covenant. Operating cash flow remained positive ($52.6M Q1 FY26) despite the $180M GAAP net loss (most of the loss is non-cash goodwill impairment). The 2023 Credit Agreement matures Feb 2028 - refinancing risk exists, but not acute. Liquidity is adequate: $59M cash + $174.9M revolver capacity = ~$234M total liquidity at Q1 FY26. Net cash provided by operating activities was $52.6M in Q1 FY26 - the operating business is cash-flow positive once impairment is backed out. This supports the insiders' purchasing thesis (GO-01).

Future Optimization Plan estimate: bad debt expense $16M for FY26 + an additional ~$0M-$3M cash IO-termination expense.  Comparing to 529 active IO stores, 36 closures = ~6.8% of the IO base in one cohort wave.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch - the IO model is celebrated in the Business section as a competitive moat but the IO-credit exposure is under-quantified in the 10-K. ~7% of the IO base is being terminated with associated bad-debt write-offs of ~$15-16M, which is the first hard signal that the IO model has structural underperformers requiring the parent to bear loan losses. If macro conditions worsen (SNAP cuts, comp store decline accelerating), more IO terminations are possible. Moderate not severe because the Optimization Plan is bounded (36 stores) and the financial magnitude is manageable on a $4.7B sales base.

summary: GO is the ANTI-CALM: a textbook ABG-pattern positive insider signal stacked against a genuinely impaired and litigated business. Six named insiders - CEO Potter ($2.4M), Lead Director Ragatz ($2.8M), Chairman Lindberg ($1.6M, reversing prior selling), and 3 other directors - clustered 15 open-market code-P purchases for $7.92M in the 21-day window after the Mar 4, 2026 10-K and Mar 2 Optimization Plan adoption, at $5.72-$7.06/sh into a 57% drawdown. Total trailing-24mo sell:buy dollar ratio is near-parity at 1.08, with the sales dominated by pre-Potter Lindberg 10b5-1 plan disposals and recent Mar 9 RSU tax-withholding (not discretionary). Operating cash flow remained positive ($52.6M Q1 FY26) and leverage is well within covenants (~1.67x vs 3.25x cap). Offsetting negatives are real: cumulative $307M of 2-quarter goodwill impairments expose the FY25 charge as a partial step-down, a NEW Mar 16, 2026 class action targets current management's restructuring narrative, Optimization Plan costs were revised upward 43%, $15.5M IO bad-debt write-off signals model stress, and comparable store sales turned -1.0% on a smaller post-closure denominator. VERDICT: LONG-tier. The insider Form-4 evidence is the strongest signal under the framework and directly contradicts the distressed price action; the impairment/restructuring/litigation overhang is largely backward-looking and quantified, while the forward setup is a new CEO + refreshed board + cash-flow-positive operating engine + aligned insider conviction at the bottom.
